response:
Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Science and Technology from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024.

Please note that the ministry's official name changed during this period, often merging with or separating from "Communications."

**1. Gilberto Kassab**
*   **Period:** In office during all of 2018 (Served from May 12, 2016 – January 1, 2019)
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations and Communications (MCTIC)
*   **President:** Michel Temer

**2. Marcos Pontes**
*   **Period:** January 1, 2019 – March 30, 2022
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations and Communications (until June 2020); Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovations (after June 2020).
*   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Note:** He left the position to run for the Senate.

**3. Paulo César Alvim**
*   **Period:** March 30, 2022 – December 31, 2022
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovations
*   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro

**4. Luciana Santos**
*   **Period:** January 1, 2023 – End of 2024 (Incumbent)
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI)
*   **President:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva

During this period, the portfolio underwent name changes, shifting from the **Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC)** to the **Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovations (MCTI)**, and finally to the singular **Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation**.

**1. Gilberto Kassab**
*   **Term Start:** May 12, 2016
*   **Term End:** January 1, 2019
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC)
*   **Administration:** Michel Temer
*   **Notes:** Kassab served through the end of the Temer administration in 2018. During his tenure, the Ministry of Science and Technology was merged with the Ministry of Communications.

**2. Marcos Pontes**
*   **Term Start:** January 1, 2019
*   **Term End:** March 30, 2022
*   **Ministry Name:**
    *   *Jan 2019–Jun 2020:* Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC)
    *   *Jun 2020–Mar 2022:* Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovations (MCTI)
*   **Administration:** Jair Bolsonaro

**3. Paulo César Alvim**

*   **Term End:** December 31, 2022
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovations (MCTI)
*   **Administration:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Notes:** A career civil servant and entrepreneurship specialist, Alvim served as the Executive Secretary (Deputy Minister) before taking over the ministry following Pontes' resignation. He served until the end of the Bolsonaro presidency.

*   **Term Start:** January 1, 2023
*   **Term End:** Present (Incumbent as of 2024)
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation
*   **Administration:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva

# Lista de ministros da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação do Brasil

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o "Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação")** do [Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil "Brasil").[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-mct-1)

## História

Esta seção é um excerto de [Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação § História](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o#História "Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação").[[editar](https://pt.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o&action=edit)]

Foi criado como Ministério da Ciência e Tecnologia (MCT) durante o governo [José Sarney](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Sarney "José Sarney") em [15 de março](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_de_mar%C3%A7o "15 de março") de [1985](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985 "1985"), pelo decreto nº 91.146, como [órgão](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%93rg%C3%A3o_p%C3%BAblico "Órgão público") central do sistema federal de [ciência](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ci%C3%AAncia "Ciência") e [tecnologia](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tecnologia "Tecnologia").[[2]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-2) O surgimento desse novo ministério, além de expressar a importância política desse segmento, atendeu a um antigo anseio da comunidade científica e tecnológica nacional.[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_mctic_historia-3)

[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/02.01.2023_-_Posse_de_Luciana_Santos%2C_Ministra_de_Estado_da_Ci%C3%AAncia_e_Tecnologia_%2852624169820%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-02.01.2023_-_Posse_de_Luciana_Santos%2C_Ministra_de_Estado_da_Ci%C3%AAncia_e_Tecnologia_%2852624169820%29_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ficheiro:02.01.2023_-_Posse_de_Luciana_Santos,_Ministra_de_Estado_da_Ci%C3%AAncia_e_Tecnologia_(52624169820)_(cropped).jpg)

*Luciana Santos, atual Ministra de Estado da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação*

Durante o período de 29 de março de 1989 a 29 de novembro de 1989, o MCT foi incorporado pelo [Ministério do Desenvolvimento da Indústria e Comércio](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Ind%C3%BAstria,_Com%C3%A9rcio_Exterior_e_Servi%C3%A7os "Ministério da Indústria, Comércio Exterior e Serviços"). Ao final deste período, foi separado e se tornou Secretaria Especial da Ciência e Tecnologia, com *status* de ministério, mantendo seu ocupante. Em 1990, foi renomeada para Secretaria da Ciência e Tecnologia, desta vez ligada à presidência da república, do então presidente [Fernando Collor de Mello](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Collor "Fernando Collor"). Em 1992, o presidente [Itamar Franco](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") retirou a secretaria da Presidência da República e recriou o ministério com o nome original.[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_mctic_historia-3)

Em 2011, com a Medida Provisória nº 541, o MCT foi renomeado para Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (MCTI).[[4]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_PRESIDÊNCIA_DA_REPÚBLICA-4)[[5]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_FAPEAM_2011-5)

Em 12 de maio de 2016, com a Medida Provisória nº 726, convertida na Lei nº 13.341, de 29 de setembro de 2016, extinguiu-se o [Ministério das Comunicações](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_das_Comunica%C3%A7%C3%B5es_(Brasil) "Ministério das Comunicações (Brasil)") e transformou o MCTI em Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia, Inovações e Comunicações (MCTIC).[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_mctic_historia-3)

Em 10 de junho de 2020, o ex-presidente [Jair Bolsonaro](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro "Jair Bolsonaro") anunciou que decidiu recriar o Ministério das Comunicações, separando-o do MCTIC, com [Fábio Faria](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A1bio_Faria_(pol%C3%ADtico) "Fábio Faria (político)") no cargo de ministro.[[6]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-6)

full_history.response:
The following is a list of the Brazilian Ministers of Science and Technology from 2018 to 2024.

During this period, the portfolio underwent name changes, shifting from the **Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC)** to the **Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovations (MCTI)**, and finally to the singular **Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation**.

### **List of Ministers (2018–2024)**

**1. Gilberto Kassab**
*   **Term Start:** May 12, 2016
*   **Term End:** January 1, 2019
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC)
*   **Administration:** Michel Temer
*   **Notes:** Kassab served through the end of the Temer administration in 2018. During his tenure, the Ministry of Science and Technology was merged with the Ministry of Communications.

**2. Marcos Pontes**
*   **Term Start:** January 1, 2019
*   **Term End:** March 30, 2022
*   **Ministry Name:**
    *   *Jan 2019–Jun 2020:* Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations, and Communications (MCTIC)
    *   *Jun 2020–Mar 2022:* Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovations (MCTI)
*   **Administration:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Notes:** Marcos Pontes, a former astronaut, was the first minister under Bolsonaro. In June 2020, the Ministry of Communications was separated again, leaving Pontes with the Science, Technology, and Innovations portfolio. He resigned in March 2022 to run for a seat in the Chamber of Deputies.

**3. Paulo César Alvim**
*   **Term Start:** March 30, 2022
*   **Term End:** December 31, 2022
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovations (MCTI)
*   **Administration:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Notes:** A career civil servant and entrepreneurship specialist, Alvim served as the Executive Secretary (Deputy Minister) before taking over the ministry following Pontes' resignation. He served until the end of the Bolsonaro presidency.

**4. Luciana Santos**
*   **Term Start:** January 1, 2023
*   **Term End:** Present (Incumbent as of 2024)
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation
*   **Administration:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
*   **Notes:** Luciana Santos assumed office at the start of Lula's third term. She is the first woman to hold this position permanently. Under her tenure, the ministry's name was slightly adjusted to the singular "Innovation" (*Inovação*).

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o "Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação")** do [Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil "Brasil").[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-mct-1)

## História

Esta seção é um excerto de [Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação § História](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o#História "Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação").[[editar](https://pt.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o&action=edit)]

Foi criado como Ministério da Ciência e Tecnologia (MCT) durante o governo [José Sarney](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Sarney "José Sarney") em [15 de março](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_de_mar%C3%A7o "15 de março") de [1985](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985 "1985"), pelo decreto nº 91.146, como [órgão](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%93rg%C3%A3o_p%C3%BAblico "Órgão público") central do sistema federal de [ciência](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ci%C3%AAncia "Ciência") e [tecnologia](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tecnologia "Tecnologia").[[2]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-2) O surgimento desse novo ministério, além de expressar a importância política desse segmento, atendeu a um antigo anseio da comunidade científica e tecnológica nacional.[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_mctic_historia-3)

[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/02.01.2023_-_Posse_de_Luciana_Santos%2C_Ministra_de_Estado_da_Ci%C3%AAncia_e_Tecnologia_%2852624169820%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-02.01.2023_-_Posse_de_Luciana_Santos%2C_Ministra_de_Estado_da_Ci%C3%AAncia_e_Tecnologia_%2852624169820%29_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ficheiro:02.01.2023_-_Posse_de_Luciana_Santos,_Ministra_de_Estado_da_Ci%C3%AAncia_e_Tecnologia_(52624169820)_(cropped).jpg)

*Luciana Santos, atual Ministra de Estado da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação*

Durante o período de 29 de março de 1989 a 29 de novembro de 1989, o MCT foi incorporado pelo [Ministério do Desenvolvimento da Indústria e Comércio](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Ind%C3%BAstria,_Com%C3%A9rcio_Exterior_e_Servi%C3%A7os "Ministério da Indústria, Comércio Exterior e Serviços"). Ao final deste período, foi separado e se tornou Secretaria Especial da Ciência e Tecnologia, com *status* de ministério, mantendo seu ocupante. Em 1990, foi renomeada para Secretaria da Ciência e Tecnologia, desta vez ligada à presidência da república, do então presidente [Fernando Collor de Mello](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Collor "Fernando Collor"). Em 1992, o presidente [Itamar Franco](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") retirou a secretaria da Presidência da República e recriou o ministério com o nome original.[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_mctic_historia-3)

Em 2011, com a Medida Provisória nº 541, o MCT foi renomeado para Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (MCTI).[[4]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_PRESIDÊNCIA_DA_REPÚBLICA-4)[[5]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_FAPEAM_2011-5)

Em 12 de maio de 2016, com a Medida Provisória nº 726, convertida na Lei nº 13.341, de 29 de setembro de 2016, extinguiu-se o [Ministério das Comunicações](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_das_Comunica%C3%A7%C3%B5es_(Brasil) "Ministério das Comunicações (Brasil)") e transformou o MCTI em Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia, Inovações e Comunicações (MCTIC).[[3]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-Ministério_da_Ciência,_Tecnologia_e_Inovação_mctic_historia-3)

Em 10 de junho de 2020, o ex-presidente [Jair Bolsonaro](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro "Jair Bolsonaro") anunciou que decidiu recriar o Ministério das Comunicações, separando-o do MCTIC, com [Fábio Faria](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A1bio_Faria_(pol%C3%ADtico) "Fábio Faria (político)") no cargo de ministro.[[6]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Ci%C3%AAncia,_Tecnologia_e_Inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o_do_Brasil#cite_note-6)

message.content:
Here is the list of the Brazilian Ministers of Science and Technology from the beginning of 2018 until the end of 2024.

During this period, the portfolio underwent name changes, notably separating from "Communications" in 2020.

**1. Gilberto Kassab**
*   **Period:** Serving in 2018 – January 1, 2019
*   **Ministry Name:** *Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia, Inovações e Comunicações* (MCTIC)
*   **Context:** He took office in 2016 under President Michel Temer and remained until the end of that administration.

**2. Marcos Pontes**
*   **Period:** January 1, 2019 – March 30, 2022
*   **Ministry Name:**
    *   *Until June 2020:* MCTIC (included Communications)
    *   *From June 2020:* *Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovações* (MCTI)
*   **Context:** Appointed by President Jair Bolsonaro. He left the post to run for the Senate.

**3. Paulo Alvim**
*   **Period:** March 30, 2022 – January 1, 2023
*   **Ministry Name:** *Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovações* (MCTI)
*   **Context:** Took over the position for the remainder of the Bolsonaro administration.

Here are the Brazilian Ministers of Science and Technology from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024.

During this period, the Ministry underwent administrative changes, particularly the separation from the Ministry of Communications in 2020.

*   **Gilberto Kassab**
    *   **Period:** Served throughout 2018 until January 1, 2019.
    *   **Government:** Michel Temer.
    *   **Context:** He held the title of Minister of Science, Technology, Innovations and Communications (MCTIC), as the portfolios were merged at the time.

*   **Marcos Pontes**
    *   **Period:** January 1, 2019 – March 30, 2022.
    *   **Government:** Jair Bolsonaro.
    *   **Context:** He began as Minister of MCTIC. In June 2020, the Ministry of Communications was recreated, and his portfolio was renamed the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovations (MCTI). He resigned in March 2022 to run for the Senate.

*   **Paulo Alvim**
    *   **Period:** March 30, 2022 – January 1, 2023.
    *   **Government:** Jair Bolsonaro.
    *   **Context:** A career civil servant who was previously the Secretary of Entrepreneurship and Innovation, he took over for the remainder of the presidential term.

*   **Luciana Santos**
    *   **Period:** January 1, 2023 – End of 2024 (Continuing in office).
    *   **Government:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
    *   **Context:** She became the first woman to permanently lead the ministry, now styled as the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

full_history.response:
Based on the official records of the Brazilian government, here is the list of Ministers of Science and Technology from 2018 to 2024.

During this period, the Ministry underwent name changes: it began as the **Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations and Communications (MCTIC)**, was split in 2020 to become the **Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovations (MCTI)**, and was renamed to the **Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation** in 2023.

### List of Ministers (2018–2024)

**1. Gilberto Kassab**
*   **Dates in Office (Total):** May 12, 2016 – January 1, 2019
*   **Period Relevant to Query:** January 1, 2018 – January 1, 2019
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations and Communications (MCTIC)
*   **Government:** Michel Temer
*   **Notes:** Served the remainder of his term through 2018.

**2. Marcos Pontes**
*   **Dates in Office:** January 1, 2019 – March 30, 2022
*   **Ministry Name:**
    *   Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovations and Communications (Jan 2019 – June 2020)
    *   Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovations (June 2020 – March 2022)*
*   **Government:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Notes:** The astronaut and engineer led the specific Science and Technology portfolio after it was separated from Communications in June 2020. He resigned in March 2022 to run for the Senate.

**3. Paulo Alvim (Paulo César Rezende de Carvalho Alvim)**
*   **Dates in Office:** March 30, 2022 – January 1, 2023
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovations (MCTI)
*   **Government:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Notes:** Previously the Secretary for Entrepreneurship and Innovation, he took over after Pontes' resignation.

**4. Luciana Santos**
*   **Dates in Office:** January 1, 2023 – Present (as of 2024)
*   **Ministry Name:** Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI)**
*   **Government:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
*   **Notes:** The first woman to permanently hold the position. The Ministry's name was slightly adjusted from the plural "Inovações" back to the singular "Inovação" at the start of her term.

***
* *Note on Ministry Split:* The Ministry of Communications was recreated on June 10, 2020, separating it from Science and Technology.
** *Note on Naming:* While often referred to by the acronym MCTI throughout this period, the official Portuguese name changed from *Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovações* (Bolsonaro era) to *Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação* (Lula era).

Based on the period from the beginning of 2018 to the end of 2024, here are the Brazilian Ministers of Planning.

It is relevant to note that between **2019 and 2022**, the Ministry of Planning did not exist as an independent entity; it was merged into the Ministry of Economy.

### **Timeline of Ministers (2018–2024)**

**1. Dyogo Oliveira**
*   **Role:** Minister of Planning, Development and Management
*   **Period:** Served from 2016 until **April 9, 2018**.
*   **Government:** Michel Temer

**2. Esteves Colnago**
*   **Role:** Minister of Planning, Development and Management
*   **Period:** **April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018**
*   **Government:** Michel Temer

---
**Merger Period (2019–2022)**
During the administration of Jair Bolsonaro, the Ministry of Planning was dissolved and its functions were absorbed by the **Ministry of Economy**, headed by **Paulo Guedes**. Technically, there was no separate "Minister of Planning" during this time. The duties were overseen by the *Special Secretariat of Finance and Budget* (Secretaria Especial de Fazenda/Tesouro e Orçamento) within the Ministry of Economy.
*   *Minister responsible:* **Paulo Guedes** (Jan 1, 2019 – Dec 31, 2022)
---

**3. Simone Tebet**
*   **Role:** Minister of Planning and Budget
*   **Period:** **January 1, 2023 – Present** (Served through the end of 2024)
*   **Government:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
*   *Note:* The ministry was re-established in 2023, distinct from the Ministry of Finance and the new Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services.

Based on the period from the beginning of 2018 to the end of 2024, here are the Brazilian Ministers of Planning.

It is relevant to note that between **2019 and 2022**, the Ministry of Planning did not exist as an independent entity; it was merged into the Ministry of Economy.

### **Timeline of Ministers (2018–2024)**

**1. Dyogo Oliveira**
*   **Role:** Minister of Planning, Development and Management
*   **Period:** Served from 2016 until **April 9, 2018**.
*   **Government:** Michel Temer

**2. Esteves Colnago**
*   **Role:** Minister of Planning, Development and Management
*   **Period:** **April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018**
*   **Government:** Michel Temer

---
**Merger Period (2019–2022)**
During the administration of Jair Bolsonaro, the Ministry of Planning was dissolved and its functions were absorbed by the **Ministry of Economy**, headed by **Paulo Guedes**. Technically, there was no separate "Minister of Planning" during this time. The duties were overseen by the *Special Secretariat of Finance and Budget* (Secretaria Especial de Fazenda/Tesouro e Orçamento) within the Ministry of Economy.
*   *Minister responsible:* **Paulo Guedes** (Jan 1, 2019 – Dec 31, 2022)
---

**3. Simone Tebet**
*   **Role:** Minister of Planning and Budget
*   **Period:** **January 1, 2023 – Present** (Served through the end of 2024)
*   **Government:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
*   *Note:* The ministry was re-established in 2023, distinct from the Ministry of Finance and the new Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services.

Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Planning (or equivalent) for the period from 2018 to 2024.

It is important to note that from January 2019 to December 2022, the Ministry of Planning was dissolved and its functions were merged into the **Ministry of Economy**. It was re-established as an independent ministry in 2023.

### List of Ministers (2018–2024)

| **Minister** | **Title** | **Term Start** | **Term End** | **President** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dyogo Oliveira** | Minister of Planning, Development and Management | May 23, 2016* | April 7, 2018 | Michel Temer |
| **Esteves Colnago** | Minister of Planning, Development and Management | April 7, 2018 | December 31, 2018 | Michel Temer |
| **Paulo Guedes** | Minister of Economy** | January 1, 2019 | December 31, 2022 | Jair Bolsonaro |
| **Simone Tebet** | Minister of Planning and Budget | January 1, 2023 | Present | Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva |

*\*Dyogo Oliveira served from 2016; his term covered the beginning of 2018.*
*\*\*During the Bolsonaro administration (2019–2022), the Ministry of Planning was merged into the "Super-Ministry" of Economy headed by Paulo Guedes.*

### Key Details

*   **2018 (Temer Administration):** The ministry existed as the **Ministry of Planning, Development and Management** (*Ministério do Planejamento, Desenvolvimento e Gestão*). **Esteves Colnago** took over in April 2018 after Dyogo Oliveira left to become the president of BNDES.
*   **2019–2022 (Bolsonaro Administration):** The ministry was extinguished, and its responsibilities fell under the **Ministry of Economy**. Within this structure, the planning and budget functions were largely handled by the **Special Secretariat of Treasury and Budget** (*Secretaria Especial de Tesouro e Orçamento*), led by secretaries such as **Waldery Rodrigues** (2019–2021), **Bruno Funchal** (2021), and **Esteves Colnago** (2021–2022). However, **Paulo Guedes** was the sole Cabinet Minister responsible.
*   **2023–2024 (Lula Administration):** The ministry was recreated as the **Ministry of Planning and Budget** (*Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento*), with remaining management functions split into a separate Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services. **Simone Tebet** was appointed as the minister.

Based on the period from the beginning of 2018 to the end of 2024, here are the Brazilian Ministers of Planning.

It is relevant to note that between **2019 and 2022**, the Ministry of Planning did not exist as an independent entity; it was merged into the Ministry of Economy.

### **Timeline of Ministers (2018–2024)**

**1. Dyogo Oliveira**
*   **Role:** Minister of Planning, Development and Management
*   **Period:** Served from 2016 until **April 9, 2018**.
*   **Government:** Michel Temer

**2. Esteves Colnago**
*   **Role:** Minister of Planning, Development and Management
*   **Period:** **April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018**
*   **Government:** Michel Temer

---
**Merger Period (2019–2022)**
During the administration of Jair Bolsonaro, the Ministry of Planning was dissolved and its functions were absorbed by the **Ministry of Economy**, headed by **Paulo Guedes**. Technically, there was no separate "Minister of Planning" during this time. The duties were overseen by the *Special Secretariat of Finance and Budget* (Secretaria Especial de Fazenda/Tesouro e Orçamento) within the Ministry of Economy.
*   *Minister responsible:* **Paulo Guedes** (Jan 1, 2019 – Dec 31, 2022)
---

**3. Simone Tebet**
*   **Role:** Minister of Planning and Budget
*   **Period:** **January 1, 2023 – Present** (Served through the end of 2024)
*   **Government:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
*   *Note:* The ministry was re-established in 2023, distinct from the Ministry of Finance and the new Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services.

Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Health who served from 2018 to 2024.

*Note: Dates marked "Incumbent" or "Through 2024" indicate the minister served through the end of the requested period.*

### **1. Ricardo Barros**
*   **Start Date:** May 12, 2016 (Serving at the start of 2018)
*   **End Date:** April 2, 2018
*   **President:** Michel Temer
*   **Notes:** Resigned to run for a seat in the Chamber of Deputies.

### **2. Gilberto Occhi**
*   **Start Date:** April 2, 2018
*   **End Date:** January 1, 2019
*   **President:** Michel Temer
*   **Notes:** Served until the end of the Temer administration.

### **3. Luiz Henrique Mandetta**
*   **Start Date:** January 1, 2019
*   **End Date:** April 16, 2020
*   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Notes:** Dismissed following disagreements with the President regarding the COVID-19 pandemic response.

### **4. Nelson Teich**
*   **Start Date:** April 17, 2020
*   **End Date:** May 15, 2020
*   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Notes:** Resigned less than a month into his term due to disagreements over hydroxychloroquine and social distancing guidelines.

### **5. Eduardo Pazuello**
*   **Start Date:** May 16, 2020 (Interim); September 16, 2020 (Official)
*   **End Date:** March 23, 2021
*   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Notes:** An innovative army general who served initially as interim minister for four months before being officially appointed.

### **6. Marcelo Queiroga**
*   **Start Date:** March 23, 2021
*   **End Date:** December 31, 2022
*   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro
*   **Notes:** A cardiologist who served until the end of the Bolsonaro administration.

### **7. Nísia Trindade**
*   **Start Date:** January 1, 2023
*   **End Date:** Served through 2024
*   **President:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
*   **Notes:** The first woman to lead the ministry. She remained in office throughout all of 2024 (leaving in early 2025).

*   **Nísia Trindade**: Took office on January 1, 2023, and remained in the position through the end of 2024.

From 2019 to 2022, during the administration of President Jair Bolsonaro, the **Ministry of Planning** (formerly *Ministério do Planejamento, Desenvolvimento e Gestão*) **did not exist as an independent ministry**.

Upon taking office on January 1, 2019, the Bolsonaro administration merged the Ministry of Planning into a new "super-ministry"—the **Ministry of Economy** (*Ministério da Economia*), led by Minister **Paulo Guedes**.

### Key Details on Status & Structure (2019–2022)

*   **Merger (Jan 2019):** Provisional Measure No. 870 (later Law No. 13.844/2019) officially extinguished the Ministry of Planning, incorporating its functions—along with those of the Ministry of Finance (*Fazenda*) and the Ministry of Industry, Foreign Trade and Services (*MDIC*)—into the Ministry of Economy.
*   **New Internal Role:** The responsibilities previously held by the Ministry of Planning (such as federal budget preparation) were reassigned to a "Special Secretariat" structure within the Ministry of Economy.
    *   **Phase 1 (2019–2021):** The functions fell under the **Special Secretariat of Finance** (*Secretaria Especial de Fazenda*), initially headed by **Waldery Rodrigues**.
    *   **Phase 2 (2021–2022):** Following a reorganization and the departure of key secretaries, a new body was created: the **Special Secretariat of Treasury and Budget** (*Secretaria Especial do Tesouro e Orçamento*). This was briefly led by **Bruno Funchal** (April–Oct 2021) and then by **Esteves Colnago** (Oct 2021–Dec 2022).
*   **Minister in Charge:** As the functions were absorbed, the ultimate authority over Brazil's planning and budget during this entire period was the Minister of Economy, **Paulo Guedes**.

### Post-2022 Context
The Ministry was re-established as an independent entity immediately following the end of the Bolsonaro administration. On January 1, 2023, the incoming Lula administration split the Ministry of Economy, recreating the **Ministry of Planning and Budget** (*Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento*).

message.content:
Based on your request, here is the list of Brazilian officials responsible for the Planning portfolio from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024.

It is important to note that the **Ministry of Planning** ceased to exist as an independent entity between 2019 and 2022, when it was merged into the Ministry of Economy.

### **2018: Temer Administration**
*Ministry Name: Ministério do Planejamento, Desenvolvimento e Gestão*

*   **Dyogo Oliveira**
    *   **Period:** Jan 1, 2018 – April 7, 2018
    *   *Note: Left to assume the presidency of BNDES.*
*   **Esteves Colnago**
    *   **Period:** April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018

### **2019 – 2022: Bolsonaro Administration**
*Ministry Name: Ministry of Economy (Ministério da Economia)*

During this period, the Ministry of Planning was **extinguished**. Its responsibilities were absorbed by the "Super-Ministry" of Economy.

*   **Paulo Guedes** (Minister of Economy)
    *   **Period:** Jan 1, 2019 – December 31, 2022
    *   *Planning functions were handled by Special Secretaries under his department, most notably Waldery Rodrigues (2019–2021) and Esteves Colnago (2021–2022), but Guedes was the Minister in charge.*

### **2023 – 2024: Lula Administration**
*Ministry Name: Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento*

The ministry was re-established as an independent body at the start of the new government.

*   **Simone Tebet**
    *   **Period:** Jan 1, 2023 – Present (through end of 2024)

full_history.response:
From 2019 to 2022, during the administration of President Jair Bolsonaro, the **Ministry of Planning** (formerly *Ministério do Planejamento, Desenvolvimento e Gestão*) **did not exist as an independent ministry**.

Upon taking office on January 1, 2019, the Bolsonaro administration merged the Ministry of Planning into a new "super-ministry"—the **Ministry of Economy** (*Ministério da Economia*), led by Minister **Paulo Guedes**.

### Key Details on Status & Structure (2019–2022)

*   **Merger (Jan 2019):** Provisional Measure No. 870 (later Law No. 13.844/2019) officially extinguished the Ministry of Planning, incorporating its functions—along with those of the Ministry of Finance (*Fazenda*) and the Ministry of Industry, Foreign Trade and Services (*MDIC*)—into the Ministry of Economy.
*   **New Internal Role:** The responsibilities previously held by the Ministry of Planning (such as federal budget preparation) were reassigned to a "Special Secretariat" structure within the Ministry of Economy.
    *   **Phase 1 (2019–2021):** The functions fell under the **Special Secretariat of Finance** (*Secretaria Especial de Fazenda*), initially headed by **Waldery Rodrigues**.
    *   **Phase 2 (2021–2022):** Following a reorganization and the departure of key secretaries, a new body was created: the **Special Secretariat of Treasury and Budget** (*Secretaria Especial do Tesouro e Orçamento*). This was briefly led by **Bruno Funchal** (April–Oct 2021) and then by **Esteves Colnago** (Oct 2021–Dec 2022).
*   **Minister in Charge:** As the functions were absorbed, the ultimate authority over Brazil's planning and budget during this entire period was the Minister of Economy, **Paulo Guedes**.

### Post-2022 Context
The Ministry was re-established as an independent entity immediately following the end of the Bolsonaro administration. On January 1, 2023, the incoming Lula administration split the Ministry of Economy, recreating the **Ministry of Planning and Budget** (*Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento*).

From 2019 to 2022, the **Ministry of Planning (Ministério do Planejamento) did not exist as an independent ministry**. At the beginning of President Jair Bolsonaro's administration (January 1, 2019), the ministry was dissolved, and its functions were merged into the newly created **Ministry of Economy (*Ministério da Economia*)**.

The functions previously held by the Ministry of Planning (such as the federal budget, national planning, and management) were absorbed primarily by a "Special Secretariat" structure within the Ministry of Economy.

### Who Was Responsible (2019–2022)

Two levels of leadership were responsible for the planning functions during this period:

**1. The Minister of Economy (The "Super Minister")**
*   **Paulo Guedes:** As the Minister of Economy for the entire 2019–2022 term, he held ultimate responsibility for the portfolios of Planning, Finance, Industry, Labor, and Trade combined.

**2. The Special Secretaries (Direct Supervisors)**
The specific responsibilities for planning and budget were delegated to a high-level secretary. The title of this position evolved slightly, but the role remained the "de facto" Planning Minister in technical terms.

*   **Waldery Rodrigues (Jan 2019 – April 2021):**
    *   **Title:** Special Secretary of Finance (*Secretário Especial de Fazenda*).
    *   **Role:** He managed the federal budget and treasury. He was replaced in early 2021 following disputes regarding the federal budget authorization.

*   **Bruno Funchal (April 2021 – Oct 2021):**
    *   **Title:** Special Secretary of Treasury and Budget (*Secretário Especial do Tesouro e Orçamento*).
    *   **Role:** The secretariat was restructured and renamed to explicitly include "Budget" in its title. Funchal resigned in October 2021 over disagreements regarding the government's decision to alter the "spending cap" (*teto de gastos*).

*   **Esteves Colnago (Oct 2021 – Dec 2022):**
    *   **Title:** Special Secretary of Treasury and Budget (*Secretário Especial do Tesouro e Orçamento*).
    *   **Role:** He took over after the resignation of Funchal and managed the country's planning and budget until the end of the Bolsonaro administration.

### Summary of Status
*   **2019–2022:** Extinguished. Merged into the Ministry of Economy.
*   **Function Holder:** Special Secretariat of Treasury and Budget (SETO) / Special Secretariat of Finance.
*   **2023–Present:** Re-established as the **Ministry of Planning and Budget (*Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento*)** under the administration of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with **Simone Tebet** appointed as minister.

full_history.response:
From 2019 to 2022, the **Ministry of Planning (Ministério do Planejamento) did not exist as an independent ministry**. At the beginning of President Jair Bolsonaro's administration (January 1, 2019), the ministry was dissolved, and its functions were merged into the newly created **Ministry of Economy (*Ministério da Economia*)**.

The functions previously held by the Ministry of Planning (such as the federal budget, national planning, and management) were absorbed primarily by a "Special Secretariat" structure within the Ministry of Economy.

### Who Was Responsible (2019–2022)

Two levels of leadership were responsible for the planning functions during this period:

**1. The Minister of Economy (The "Super Minister")**
*   **Paulo Guedes:** As the Minister of Economy for the entire 2019–2022 term, he held ultimate responsibility for the portfolios of Planning, Finance, Industry, Labor, and Trade combined.

**2. The Special Secretaries (Direct Supervisors)**
The specific responsibilities for planning and budget were delegated to a high-level secretary. The title of this position evolved slightly, but the role remained the "de facto" Planning Minister in technical terms.

*   **Waldery Rodrigues (Jan 2019 – April 2021):**
    *   **Title:** Special Secretary of Finance (*Secretário Especial de Fazenda*).
    *   **Role:** He managed the federal budget and treasury. He was replaced in early 2021 following disputes regarding the federal budget authorization.

*   **Bruno Funchal (April 2021 – Oct 2021):**
    *   **Title:** Special Secretary of Treasury and Budget (*Secretário Especial do Tesouro e Orçamento*).
    *   **Role:** The secretariat was restructured and renamed to explicitly include "Budget" in its title. Funchal resigned in October 2021 over disagreements regarding the government's decision to alter the "spending cap" (*teto de gastos*).

*   **Esteves Colnago (Oct 2021 – Dec 2022):**
    *   **Title:** Special Secretary of Treasury and Budget (*Secretário Especial do Tesouro e Orçamento*).
    *   **Role:** He took over after the resignation of Funchal and managed the country's planning and budget until the end of the Bolsonaro administration.

### Summary of Status
*   **2019–2022:** Extinguished. Merged into the Ministry of Economy.
*   **Function Holder:** Special Secretariat of Treasury and Budget (SETO) / Special Secretariat of Finance.
*   **2023–Present:** Re-established as the **Ministry of Planning and Budget (*Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento*)** under the administration of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with **Simone Tebet** appointed as minister.

*   **Paulo Guedes:** As the Minister of Economy for the entire 2019–2022 term, he held ultimate responsibility for the portfolios of Planning, Finance, Industry, Labor, and Trade combined.

**2. The Special Secretaries (Direct Supervisors)**
The specific responsibilities for planning and budget were delegated to a high-level secretary. The title of this position evolved slightly, but the role remained the "de facto" Planning Minister in technical terms.

*   **Waldery Rodrigues (Jan 2019 – April 2021):**
    *   **Title:** Special Secretary of Finance (*Secretário Especial de Fazenda*).
    *   **Role:** He managed the federal budget and treasury. He was replaced in early 2021 following disputes regarding the federal budget authorization.

*   **Bruno Funchal (April 2021 – Oct 2021):**
    *   **Title:** Special Secretary of Treasury and Budget (*Secretário Especial do Tesouro e Orçamento*).
    *   **Role:** The secretariat was restructured and renamed to explicitly include "Budget" in its title. Funchal resigned in October 2021 over disagreements regarding the government's decision to alter the "spending cap" (*teto de gastos*).

*   **Esteves Colnago (Oct 2021 – Dec 2022):**
    *   **Title:** Special Secretary of Treasury and Budget (*Secretário Especial do Tesouro e Orçamento*).
    *   **Role:** He took over after the resignation of Funchal and managed the country's planning and budget until the end of the Bolsonaro administration.

### Summary of Status
*   **2019–2022:** Extinguished. Merged into the Ministry of Economy.
*   **Function Holder:** Special Secretariat of Treasury and Budget (SETO) / Special Secretariat of Finance.
*   **2023–Present:** Re-established as the **Ministry of Planning and Budget (*Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento*)** under the administration of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with **Simone Tebet** appointed as minister.

# Simone Tebet afirma que deixará Ministério do Planejamento até 30 de março

A ministra **Simone Tebet** (MDB) afirmou que deve deixar o **Ministério do Planejamento** até o dia 30 de março e que discutiu com o presidente **Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva** (PT) a ida dela ao Senado federal. A declaração ocorreu em evento na Insper, em São Paulo, nesta sexta-feira (30).

Tebet disse que conversou com o presidente sobre sua saída e que ele entende ser importante a participação da ministra nas [eleições de 2026](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/lula-define-prioridade-e-ministros-disputarao-senado/). A definição sobre a mudança da ministra deve ocorrer na semana que vem.

"Deixo o Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento até o dia 30 de março, quando o presidente definir, porque o presidente entende que eu sou importante no processo eleitoral, acho importante a minha candidatura", afirmou em conversa com jornalistas.

Leia Mais

-

[PSB tem tratado sobre convite a Tebet, diz João Campos à CNN](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/politica/psb-tem-tratado-sobre-convite-a-tebet-diz-joao-campos-a-cnn/)

*[PSB tem tratado sobre convite a Tebet, diz João Campos à CNN](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/politica/psb-tem-tratado-sobre-convite-a-tebet-diz-joao-campos-a-cnn/)*

-

[Por eleições, Lula avalia promover mudanças partidárias de Tebet e Marina](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/blogs/gustavo-uribe/politica/por-eleicoes-lula-avalia-promover-mudancas-partidarias-de-tebet-e-marina/)

*[Por eleições, Lula avalia promover mudanças partidárias de Tebet e Marina](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/blogs/gustavo-uribe/politica/por-eleicoes-lula-avalia-promover-mudancas-partidarias-de-tebet-e-marina/)*

-

[Prerrogativas recebe Tebet e quer articular candidatura em SP](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/blogs/pedro-venceslau/politica/prerrogativas-recebe-tebet-e-quer-articular-candidatura-em-sp/)

*[Prerrogativas recebe Tebet e quer articular candidatura em SP](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/blogs/pedro-venceslau/politica/prerrogativas-recebe-tebet-e-quer-articular-candidatura-em-sp/)*

Tebet começou a discutir a [candidatura dela ao Senado federal](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/blogs/pedro-venceslau/politica/tebet-vira-opcao-para-o-pt-no-senado-em-sp/) com Lula, mas não cravou qual estado ela representaria. Ambos conversaram sobre o cenário de "incerteza internacional", assim como o político e econômico do Brasil para verificar onde a parlamentar se encaixaria melhor para "cumprir sua missão".

"Para mim, política é missão, sempre foi. Eu sempre abri mão muitas vezes daquilo que eu achava que deveria fazer para cumprir missão em nome do meu partido, em nome do meu estado", disse.

Tebet ainda afirmou que não discutiu com Lula se disputará uma [vaga para o Senado](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/politica/em-sp-tebet-e-alckmin-lideram-cenarios-para-o-senado-aponta-atlas/) por São Paulo. "Não chegamos nesse detalhe. Eu me coloquei à disposição do presidente", pontuou.

## Saída de ministros de Lula

[Cerca de 20 ministros devem deixar o governo até abril para disputar as eleições](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/alem-de-gleisi-lula-deve-perder-cerca-de-20-ministros-para-as-eleicoes/). Segundo apurou a **CNN**, a tendência, neste momento, é que os secretários-executivos sejam alçados a ministros com o objetivo de manter o andamento das pastas.

Parte do primeiro escalão de Lula já foi a público confirmar a decision, enquanto outros nomes seguem em negociações nos bastidores.

Para os cargos de senador, deputado federal e governador, os ministros de Estado têm até seis meses antes do pleito para deixar os postos que ocupam atualmente, conforme determina a legislação eleitoral.

**Com informações de Pedro Venceslau e Jussara Soares, da CNN Brasil*

Here is the list of those responsible for the portfolio of Planning in Brazil from the beginning of 2018 to the end of 2024.

Please note that **between 2019 and 2022**, the Ministry of Planning did not exist as an independent entity; it was merged into the Ministry of Economy. During that period, the Minister of Economy held the primary responsibility, while specific "Special Secretaries" managed the planning and budget functions.

### **2018: Michel Temer Administration**
During this year, the portfolio was known as the **Ministry of Planning, Development, and Management**.

*   **Dyogo Oliveira**
    *   **Period:** Served until April 9, 2018.
    *   *Note:* He left the ministry to become the president of the BNDES.
*   **Esteves Colnago**
    *   **Period:** April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018.

---

*The Ministry of Planning was dissolved and absorbed into the **Ministry of Economy**.*

*   **Paulo Guedes** (Minister of Economy)
    *   **Period:** January 1, 2019 – December 31, 2022.
    *   *Context:* As the "Super Minister" of Economy, he held ultimate responsibility for Planning.

    *During this specific period, the technical "de facto" planning ministers were the Special Secretaries subordinate to Guedes:*

    *   *Bruno Funchal (Special Secretary of Treasury and Budget, 2021)*
    *   *Esteves Colnago (Special Secretary of Treasury and Budget, 2021–2022)*

---

The ministry was re-established as the **Ministry of Planning and Budget** (*Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento*).

*   **Simone Tebet**

Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Health who served from 2018 through 2024, including their specific dates of office.

This period encompasses the final year of the Michel Temer administration, the entirety of the Jair Bolsonaro administration, and the first two years of the Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva administration.

1.  **Ricardo Barros**
    *   **In office:** (Since May 12, 2016) – **April 2, 2018**
    *   **President:** Michel Temer
    *   *Note: He resigned in April 2018 to run for parliamentary re-election.*

2.  **Gilberto Occhi**
    *   **In office:** **April 2, 2018** – **January 1, 2019**
    *   **President:** Michel Temer

3.  **Luiz Henrique Mandetta**
    *   **In office:** **January 1, 2019** – **April 16, 2020**
    *   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro
    *   *Note: Dismissed following disagreements with the president regarding the management of the COVID-19 pandemic.*

4.  **Nelson Teich**
    *   **In office:** **April 17, 2020** – **May 15, 2020**
    *   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro
    *   *Note: Resigned after less than a month in office.*

5.  **Eduardo Pazuello**
    *   **In office:** **May 15, 2020** – **March 23, 2021**
    *   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro
    *   *Note: Served as interim minister from May 15, 2020, to September 16, 2020, before being officially appointed.*

6.  **Marcelo Queiroga**
    *   **In office:** **March 23, 2021** – **January 1, 2023**
    *   **President:** Jair Bolsonaro

7.  **Nísia Trindade**
    *   **In office:** **January 1, 2023** – **Present (Served throughout 2024)**
    *   **President:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
    *   *Note: She is the first woman to perform the role of Minister of Health in Brazil.*

The **Ministry of Education** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação*), commonly known as **MEC**, originates from its previous name, the **Ministry of Education and Culture** (Portuguese: *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*), is a [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil")-level [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_institutions_of_Brazil "List of federal institutions of Brazil") of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federative_Republic_of_Brazil "Federative Republic of Brazil").

Its responsibilities include coordinating national [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education "Education") policies and managing daily affairs, covering from early childhood education to post-graduate levels.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-2)

## History of the institution

Before 1930, matters related to education were the responsibility of the *National Department of Education* ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Departamento Nacional do Ensino*), which was part of the [Ministry of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_and_Public_Security_(Brazil) "Ministry of Justice and Public Security (Brazil)") at the time.

In 1930, as [Getúlio Vargas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get%C3%BAlio_Vargas "Getúlio Vargas") took office as [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Brazil "President of Brazil"), the **Ministry of Education and Public Health** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Saúde Pública*) was established, taking away education matters from the Ministry of Justice.

In 1953, the ministry was split into two: the [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Brazil) "Ministry of Health (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education and Culture** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*, with the acronym *MEC*, which lasts to this day).

In 1985, during [José Sarney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Sarney "José Sarney")'s presidency, it was again split into two: the [Ministry of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_(Brazil) "Ministry of Culture (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education**.

In 1992, as [Itamar Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") took office as president, sports were made part of the ministry again, which was subsequently renamed **Ministry of Education and Sports** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e do Desporto*).

In 1995, during [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso")'s presidency, that was once again changed, separating the **Ministry of Education** from the then [Ministry of Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Sports_(Brazil) "Ministry of Sports (Brazil)").

The incumbent Education Minister is senator [Camilo Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camilo_Santana "Camilo Santana").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-3)

Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Education who served from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024.

This period encompasses the end of the Michel Temer administration, the entire Jair Bolsonaro administration, and the beginning of the Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva administration.

### **Michel Temer Administration (2018)**
*   **Mendonça Filho**
    *   *Period:* Serving at start of 2018 – April 6, 2018
    *   *Role:* Left office to run in the 2018 elections.
*   **Rossieli Soares**
    *   *Period:* April 6, 2018 – December 31, 2018

### **Jair Bolsonaro Administration (2019–2022)**
*   **Ricardo Vélez Rodríguez**
    *   *Period:* January 1, 2019 – April 8, 2019
*   **Abraham Weintraub**
    *   *Period:* April 8, 2019 – June 20, 2020
*   **Antonio Paulo Vogel** (Interim)
    *   *Period:* June 20, 2020 – July 16, 2020
    *   *Note:* He assumed the role temporarily after Weintraub's resignation. During this interim period, **Carlos Decotelli** was named Minister (June 25) but resigned (June 30) before officially taking office due to inconsistencies in his academic resume.
*   **Milton Ribeiro**
    *   *Period:* July 16, 2020 – March 28, 2022
*   **Victor Godoy**
    *   *Period:* March 29, 2022 – December 31, 2022
    *   *Role:* Started as interim, then officially appointed on April 14, 2022.

### **Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva Administration (2023–2024)**
*   **Camilo Santana**
    *   *Period:* January 1, 2023 – End of 2024 (Incumbent role continued)

The **Ministry of Education** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação*), commonly known as **MEC**, originates from its previous name, the **Ministry of Education and Culture** (Portuguese: *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*), is a [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil")-level [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_institutions_of_Brazil "List of federal institutions of Brazil") of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federative_Republic_of_Brazil "Federative Republic of Brazil").

Its responsibilities include coordinating national [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education "Education") policies and managing daily affairs, covering from early childhood education to post-graduate levels.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-2)

## History of the institution

Before 1930, matters related to education were the responsibility of the *National Department of Education* ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Departamento Nacional do Ensino*), which was part of the [Ministry of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_and_Public_Security_(Brazil) "Ministry of Justice and Public Security (Brazil)") at the time.

In 1930, as [Getúlio Vargas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get%C3%BAlio_Vargas "Getúlio Vargas") took office as [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Brazil "President of Brazil"), the **Ministry of Education and Public Health** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Saúde Pública*) was established, taking away education matters from the Ministry of Justice.

In 1953, the ministry was split into two: the [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Brazil) "Ministry of Health (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education and Culture** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*, with the acronym *MEC*, which lasts to this day).

In 1985, during [José Sarney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Sarney "José Sarney")'s presidency, it was again split into two: the [Ministry of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_(Brazil) "Ministry of Culture (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education**.

In 1992, as [Itamar Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") took office as president, sports were made part of the ministry again, which was subsequently renamed **Ministry of Education and Sports** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e do Desporto*).

In 1995, during [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso")'s presidency, that was once again changed, separating the **Ministry of Education** from the then [Ministry of Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Sports_(Brazil) "Ministry of Sports (Brazil)").

The incumbent Education Minister is senator [Camilo Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camilo_Santana "Camilo Santana").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-3)

# Lista de ministros da Agricultura do Brasil

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros da Agricultura e Pecuária](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Agricultura_e_Pecu%C3%A1ria "Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária")** do [Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil "Brasil").[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Agricultura_do_Brasil#cite_note-ministerio-1)

Até 1892, com a denominação de Secretaria de Estado dos Negócios da Agricultura, Comércio e Obras Públicas, tinha responsabilidades tanto sobre a [agricultura](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultura "Agricultura") quanto o [transporte](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transporte "Transporte"), por isso a [lista de Ministros dos Transportes do Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_dos_Transportes_do_Brasil "Lista de ministros dos Transportes do Brasil") repete o nome dos ministros da Agricultura até 1892.[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Agricultura_do_Brasil#cite_note-ministerio-1)

When you receive a query, analyze it and break it down into focused sub-queries that can be answered independently. 
Be aware that you can create new sub-queries based on the information you receive from the subagents, your objective is to be as complete as possible.
For example, for a original question such as 'who were the top 5 most popular actors of the year 2025, how old are each of them?' you can first ask the subagent to find the top 5 most popular actors of the year 2025, and then ask the subagent to find the age of each of them separately.
Use the delegate_to_subagent function to send each sub-query to a subagent that will search for information and provide answers.
After receiving answers from subagents, synthesize the information to provide a comprehensive final answer to the user's original query.
Can you list for me all the brazilian ministers of agriculture from the beginning of 2018 until the end of 2024

Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Agriculture who served from 2018 to 2024, including their start and end dates.

*   **Blairo Maggi**
    *   **Start Date**: May 12, 2016
    *   **End Date**: January 1, 2019
    *   *Note*: Served during the Michel Temer administration. He was the incumbent minister when 2018 began.

*   **Tereza Cristina**
    *   **Start Date**: January 1, 2019
    *   **End Date**: March 30, 2022
    *   *Note*: Served during the Jair Bolsonaro administration. She left the position to run for the Senate.

*   **Marcos Montes**
    *   **Start Date**: March 30, 2022
    *   **End Date**: December 31, 2022
    *   *Note*: Served the remainder of the Bolsonaro term after Tereza Cristina's departure.

*   **Carlos Fávaro**
    *   **Start Date**: January 1, 2023
    *   **End Date**: Present (Incumbent as of 2024)
    *   *Note*: Appointed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

# Lista de ministros da Agricultura do Brasil

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros da Agricultura e Pecuária](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Agricultura_e_Pecu%C3%A1ria "Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária")** do [Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil "Brasil").[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Agricultura_do_Brasil#cite_note-ministerio-1)

Até 1892, com a denominação de Secretaria de Estado dos Negócios da Agricultura, Comércio e Obras Públicas, tinha responsabilidades tanto sobre a [agricultura](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultura "Agricultura") quanto o [transporte](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transporte "Transporte"), por isso a [lista de Ministros dos Transportes do Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_dos_Transportes_do_Brasil "Lista de ministros dos Transportes do Brasil") repete o nome dos ministros da Agricultura até 1892.[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Agricultura_do_Brasil#cite_note-ministerio-1)

The **Ministry of Education** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação*), commonly known as **MEC**, originates from its previous name, the **Ministry of Education and Culture** (Portuguese: *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*), is a [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil")-level [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_institutions_of_Brazil "List of federal institutions of Brazil") of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federative_Republic_of_Brazil "Federative Republic of Brazil").

Its responsibilities include coordinating national [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education "Education") policies and managing daily affairs, covering from early childhood education to post-graduate levels.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-2)

## History of the institution

Before 1930, matters related to education were the responsibility of the *National Department of Education* ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Departamento Nacional do Ensino*), which was part of the [Ministry of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_and_Public_Security_(Brazil) "Ministry of Justice and Public Security (Brazil)") at the time.

In 1930, as [Getúlio Vargas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get%C3%BAlio_Vargas "Getúlio Vargas") took office as [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Brazil "President of Brazil"), the **Ministry of Education and Public Health** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Saúde Pública*) was established, taking away education matters from the Ministry of Justice.

In 1953, the ministry was split into two: the [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Brazil) "Ministry of Health (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education and Culture** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*, with the acronym *MEC*, which lasts to this day).

In 1985, during [José Sarney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Sarney "José Sarney")'s presidency, it was again split into two: the [Ministry of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_(Brazil) "Ministry of Culture (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education**.

In 1992, as [Itamar Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") took office as president, sports were made part of the ministry again, which was subsequently renamed **Ministry of Education and Sports** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e do Desporto*).

In 1995, during [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso")'s presidency, that was once again changed, separating the **Ministry of Education** from the then [Ministry of Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Sports_(Brazil) "Ministry of Sports (Brazil)").

The incumbent Education Minister is senator [Camilo Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camilo_Santana "Camilo Santana").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-3)

message.content:
Here are the Brazilian Ministers of Education (**Ministros da Educação**) who served from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024.

This period covers three different presidencies: the end of Michel Temer's term, the full term of Jair Bolsonaro, and the first two years of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's third term.

### **Presidency of Michel Temer (2016–2018)**
1.  **Mendonça Filho**
    *   **Period:** Served from 2016 until **April 6, 2018**.
    *   *Context:* He was the minister at the start of 2018 but resigned in April to run for the general elections.
2.  **Rossieli Soares**
    *   **Period:** **April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018**.
    *   *Context:* Previously the Secretary of Basic Education, he served until the end of the Temer government.

### **Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro (2019–2022)**
3.  **Ricardo Vélez Rodríguez**
    *   **Period:** **January 1, 2019 – April 8, 2019**.
    *   *Context:* The first minister of the Bolsonaro administration; he remained in office for just over three months.
4.  **Abraham Weintraub**
    *   **Period:** **April 9, 2019 – June 19, 2020**.
    *   *Context:* Left office amidst controversies and investigations.
    *   *(Note: **Antonio Paulo Vogel** served as Interim Minister briefly from June 20 to July 16, 2020).*
    *   *(Note: **Carlos Alberto Decotelli** was appointed on June 25, 2020, but resigned on June 30, 2020, before officially taking office, due to inconsistencies in his academic curriculum).*
5.  **Milton Ribeiro**
    *   **Period:** **July 16, 2020 – March 28, 2022**.
    *   *Context:* A Presbyterian pastor and lawyer; he resigned following allegations of influence peddling.

The **Ministry of Education** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação*), commonly known as **MEC**, originates from its previous name, the **Ministry of Education and Culture** (Portuguese: *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*), is a [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil")-level [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_institutions_of_Brazil "List of federal institutions of Brazil") of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federative_Republic_of_Brazil "Federative Republic of Brazil").

Its responsibilities include coordinating national [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education "Education") policies and managing daily affairs, covering from early childhood education to post-graduate levels.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-2)

## History of the institution

Before 1930, matters related to education were the responsibility of the *National Department of Education* ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Departamento Nacional do Ensino*), which was part of the [Ministry of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_and_Public_Security_(Brazil) "Ministry of Justice and Public Security (Brazil)") at the time.

In 1930, as [Getúlio Vargas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get%C3%BAlio_Vargas "Getúlio Vargas") took office as [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Brazil "President of Brazil"), the **Ministry of Education and Public Health** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Saúde Pública*) was established, taking away education matters from the Ministry of Justice.

In 1953, the ministry was split into two: the [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Brazil) "Ministry of Health (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education and Culture** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*, with the acronym *MEC*, which lasts to this day).

In 1985, during [José Sarney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Sarney "José Sarney")'s presidency, it was again split into two: the [Ministry of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_(Brazil) "Ministry of Culture (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education**.

In 1992, as [Itamar Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") took office as president, sports were made part of the ministry again, which was subsequently renamed **Ministry of Education and Sports** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e do Desporto*).

In 1995, during [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso")'s presidency, that was once again changed, separating the **Ministry of Education** from the then [Ministry of Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Sports_(Brazil) "Ministry of Sports (Brazil)").

The incumbent Education Minister is senator [Camilo Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camilo_Santana "Camilo Santana").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-3)

message.content:
Here are the Brazilian Ministers of Education (**Ministros da Educação**) who served from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024.

This period covers three different presidencies: the end of Michel Temer's term, the full term of Jair Bolsonaro, and the first two years of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's third term.

### **Presidency of Michel Temer (2016–2018)**
1.  **Mendonça Filho**
    *   **Period:** Served from 2016 until **April 6, 2018**.
    *   *Context:* He was the minister at the start of 2018 but resigned in April to run for the general elections.
2.  **Rossieli Soares**
    *   **Period:** **April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018**.
    *   *Context:* Previously the Secretary of Basic Education, he served until the end of the Temer government.

### **Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro (2019–2022)**
3.  **Ricardo Vélez Rodríguez**
    *   **Period:** **January 1, 2019 – April 8, 2019**.
    *   *Context:* The first minister of the Bolsonaro administration; he remained in office for just over three months.
4.  **Abraham Weintraub**
    *   **Period:** **April 9, 2019 – June 19, 2020**.
    *   *Context:* Left office amidst controversies and investigations.
    *   *(Note: **Antonio Paulo Vogel** served as Interim Minister briefly from June 20 to July 16, 2020).*
    *   *(Note: **Carlos Alberto Decotelli** was appointed on June 25, 2020, but resigned on June 30, 2020, before officially taking office, due to inconsistencies in his academic curriculum).*
5.  **Milton Ribeiro**
    *   **Period:** **July 16, 2020 – March 28, 2022**.
    *   *Context:* A Presbyterian pastor and lawyer; he resigned following allegations of influence peddling.
6.  **Victor Godoy Veiga**
    *   **Period:** **March 29, 2022 – December 31, 2022**.
    *   *Context:* Initially the Executive Secretary, he assumed the role of interim minister and later full minister for the remainder of the presidential term.

### **Presidency of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (2023–Present)**
7.  **Camilo Santana**
    *   **Period:** **January 1, 2023 – Present** (Through the end of 2024).
    *   *Context:* Former Governor of Ceará, he has held the position since the beginning of the current administration.

# Lista de ministros da Agricultura do Brasil

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros da Agricultura e Pecuária](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_da_Agricultura_e_Pecu%C3%A1ria "Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária")** do [Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil "Brasil").[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Agricultura_do_Brasil#cite_note-ministerio-1)

Até 1892, com a denominação de Secretaria de Estado dos Negócios da Agricultura, Comércio e Obras Públicas, tinha responsabilidades tanto sobre a [agricultura](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultura "Agricultura") quanto o [transporte](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transporte "Transporte"), por isso a [lista de Ministros dos Transportes do Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_dos_Transportes_do_Brasil "Lista de ministros dos Transportes do Brasil") repete o nome dos ministros da Agricultura até 1892.[[1]](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lista_de_ministros_da_Agricultura_do_Brasil#cite_note-ministerio-1)

The **Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária*, abbreviated **MAPA**) is a [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") department in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"). The jurisdiction of this ministry is to formulate and implement policies for [agribusiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agribusiness "Agribusiness") development, integrating the aspects of market, technological, organizational and environmental care for the consumers of the country and abroad, promoting [food security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_security "Food security"), income generation and employment, reducing inequalities and increasing social inclusion.

The Ministry was founded during the [Brazilian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Empire "Brazilian Empire") in 1860. Originally named *Secretaria de Estado dos Negócios da Agricultura, Comércio e Obras Públicas*, the body was extinguished in the early years of the [First Brazilian Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Brazilian_Republic "First Brazilian Republic") and re-established in 1906 as the *Ministerio dos Negocios da Agricultura, Industria e Commercio*.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-2) In 1930, it was renamed the *Ministério da Agricultura*.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-3)

## Agroenergy

Brazil is the world leader in producing agroenergy and the Ministry of Agriculture encourages policies which develop [ethanol fuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethanol_fuel "Ethanol fuel") production.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-4)

Despite these interruptions, he remained the primary officeholder of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (*Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária*) for the year, returning to the post after each brief legislative stint.

The **Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária*, abbreviated **MAPA**) is a [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") department in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"). The jurisdiction of this ministry is to formulate and implement policies for [agribusiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agribusiness "Agribusiness") development, integrating the aspects of market, technological, organizational and environmental care for the consumers of the country and abroad, promoting [food security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_security "Food security"), income generation and employment, reducing inequalities and increasing social inclusion.

The Ministry was founded during the [Brazilian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Empire "Brazilian Empire") in 1860. Originally named *Secretaria de Estado dos Negócios da Agricultura, Comércio e Obras Públicas*, the body was extinguished in the early years of the [First Brazilian Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Brazilian_Republic "First Brazilian Republic") and re-established in 1906 as the *Ministerio dos Negocios da Agricultura, Industria e Commercio*.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-2) In 1930, it was renamed the *Ministério da Agricultura*.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-3)

## Agroenergy

Brazil is the world leader in producing agroenergy and the Ministry of Agriculture encourages policies which develop [ethanol fuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethanol_fuel "Ethanol fuel") production.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_(Brazil)#cite_note-4)

full_history.response:
Carlos Fávaro **did not** remain the Brazilian Minister of Agriculture **continuously throughout all of 2024**. While he held the position for the vast majority of the year, he was temporarily exonerated (dismissed) from the post on multiple occasions to resume his seat as a Senator in the National Congress.

This is a common political practice in Brazil known as a "temporary exoneration" (*exoneração temporária*). Ministers who are elected lawmakers often step down for brief periods (usually a few days) to cast votes on crucial legislative matters or to preserve political alliances, before being reappointed to the ministry.

**Key instances of his temporary departure in 2024 included:**

*   **May/June 2024:** Fávaro was exonerated around late May (specifically May 31, 2024) to participate in voting sessions in the Senate, such as the analysis of presidential vetoes or key amendments. He was reappointed shortly thereafter.
*   **December 2024:** He was exonerated in early December (around December 2–4) and again in mid-December (around December 18–19) to reinforce the government's base in the Senate for important year-end votes, including budget discussions and amendments.

Despite these interruptions, he remained the primary officeholder of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (*Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária*) for the year, returning to the post after each brief legislative stint.
