Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Education (**Ministros da Educação**) who served from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024, organized by presidential administration.

### **Under President Michel Temer (2018)**
From the start of 2018 until the end of the Temer government.

*   **Mendonça Filho**
    *   **Tenure:** Served from May 2016 until **April 6, 2018**.
    *   *Note:* He left the ministry to run for office in the 2018 elections.
*   **Rossieli Soares**
    *   **Tenure:** **April 6, 2018** – **December 31, 2018**.
    *   *Note:* Previously the Secretary of Basic Education, he led the ministry until the inauguration of the next government.

---

### **Under President Jair Bolsonaro (2019–2022)**
A period marked by high turnover in the ministry.

*   **Ricardo Vélez Rodríguez**
    *   **Tenure:** **January 1, 2019** – **April 8, 2019**.
*   **Abraham Weintraub**
    *   **Tenure:** **April 9, 2019** – **June 19, 2020**.
*   **Antonio Paulo Vogel** (Interim)
    *   **Tenure:** **June 20, 2020** – **July 16, 2020**.
    *   *Note on Carlos Alberto Decotelli:* Decotelli was appointed to succeed Weintraub on June 25, 2020, but resigned on June 30 due to controversies regarding his academic credentials. **He never took office**, so Vogel remained as interim during this gap.
*   **Milton Ribeiro**
    *   **Tenure:** **July 16, 2020** – **March 28, 2022**.
*   **Victor Godoy Veiga**
    *   **Tenure:** **March 29, 2022** – **December 31, 2022**.
    *   *Note:* He began as interim minister and was officially appointed as the titular minister on April 18, 2022.

---

### **Under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (2023–2024)**
From the start of Lula's third term through the end of 2024.

*   **Camilo Santana**
    *   **Tenure:** **January 1, 2023** – **Present (End of 2024)**.
    *   *Note:* A former Governor of Ceará, he has held the position continuously since the start of the administration.

The Ministry of Education (MEC) saw frequent turnover during this period, with four official ministers and one appointee who resigned before taking office.

*   **Term:** January 1, 2019 – April 8, 2019

Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Education who served under President Jair Bolsonaro from 2019 to 2022.

The Ministry of Education (MEC) saw frequent turnover during this period, with four official ministers and one appointee who resigned before taking office.

### **1. Ricardo Vélez Rodríguez**
*   **Term:** January 1, 2019 – April 8, 2019
*   **Background:** A Colombian-Brazilian philosopher and professor emeritus. He was the first education minister of the Bolsonaro administration but was dismissed after roughly three months amidst internal disputes and management issues within the ministry.

### **2. Abraham Weintraub**
*   **Term:** April 9, 2019 – June 19, 2020
*   **Background:** An economist and professor at the Federal University of São Paulo (Unifesp). His tenure was marked by significant controversies and confrontations with universities and the Supreme Federal Court (STF). He resigned in June 2020 to take a position at the World Bank.
*   *Note:* The government officially rectified his exoneration date to June 19, 2020, though he left the country shortly after his resignation announcement.

### **(Interim) Antonio Paulo Vogel**
*   **Term:** June 20, 2020 – July 16, 2020
*   **Role:** Served as the interim minister in his capacity as Executive Secretary of the MEC during the transition period between Weintraub and Ribeiro (which included the failed appointment of Carlos Decotelli).

### **(*Appointee*) Carlos Alberto Decotelli**
*   **Appointed:** June 25, 2020
*   **Resigned:** June 30, 2020
*   **Status:** **Did not take office.**
*   **Details:** Decotelli was appointed to succeed Weintraub but faced scrutiny regarding inconsistencies in his academic curriculum (including a disputed doctorate and post-doctorate). He resigned five days after his appointment without ever being sworn in.

### **3. Milton Ribeiro**
*   **Term:** July 16, 2020 – March 28, 2022
*   **Background:** A Presbyterian pastor, theologian, and lawyer. He led the ministry for nearly two years. He resigned in March 2022 following allegations of an influence-peddling scheme involving the distribution of education funds to municipalities.

### **4. Victor Godoy Veiga**
*   **Term:** March 29, 2022 – December 31, 2022
*   **Role:** Initially appointed as **Interim Minister** (published March 30) after serving as Executive Secretary under Milton Ribeiro. He was officially appointed as the full Minister of Education on April 18, 2022, and served until the end of the Bolsonaro presidency.

From the start of 2018 until the end of the Temer government.

    *   **Tenure:** Served from May 2016 until **April 6, 2018**.
    *   *Note:* He left the ministry to run for office in the 2018 elections.

    *   **Tenure:** **April 6, 2018** – **December 31, 2018**.

A period marked by high turnover in the ministry.

    *   **Tenure:** **January 1, 2019** – **April 8, 2019**.

    *   **Tenure:** **April 9, 2019** – **June 19, 2020**.

    *   **Tenure:** **July 16, 2020** – **March 28, 2022**.

    *   **Tenure:** **March 29, 2022** – **December 31, 2022**.

---

From the start of Lula's third term through the end of 2024.

*   **Camilo Santana**

# Lista de ministros do Turismo do Brasil

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros do Turismo](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_do_Turismo_(Brasil) "Ministério do Turismo (Brasil)")** do [Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil "Brasil").

De 19 de outubro de 1992, no governo do presidente [Itamar Franco](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") até o início do segundo governo do presidente [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso"), em 1 de janeiro de 1999, o ministério era denominado Ministério de Indústria, Comércio e Turismo. A partir de então foi denominado Ministério do Esporte e Turismo, até o início do primeiro mandato do presidente [Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva"), em 1 de janeiro de 2003, quando foi denominado simplesmente Ministério do Turismo.

Based on the official records and government publications, here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Tourism from **2018 to 2024**:

### **Presidency of Michel Temer (2016–2018)**
*   **Marx Beltrão**
    *   **Term:** October 5, 2016 – April 6, 2018
    *   *Note: He left the ministry in early April 2018 to run for the legislative elections.*
*   **Vinicius Lummertz**
    *   **Term:** April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018
    *   *Note: Previously the president of Embratur, he served until the end of the Temer administration.*

### **Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro (2019–2022)**
*   **Marcelo Álvaro Antônio**
    *   **Term:** January 1, 2019 – December 9, 2020
    *   *Note: Available from the first day of the government until he was dismissed in late 2020.*
*   **Gilson Machado Neto**
    *   **Term:** December 9, 2020 – March 31, 2022
    *   *Note: Often referred to as Gilson Machado. He left the post to run for the Senate.*
*   **Carlos Brito**
    *   **Term:** March 31, 2022 – December 31, 2022
    *   *Note: Former president of Embratur, he finished the term of the Bolsonaro government.*

### **Presidency of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (2023–Present)**
*   **Daniela Carneiro** (also known as Daniela do Waguinho)
    *   **Term:** January 1, 2023 – July 14, 2023
    *   *Note: She was the first minister of tourism in Lula's third term. Her dismissal was published in the Official Gazette (DOU) on July 14.*
*   **Celso Sabino**
    *   **Term:** July 14, 2023 – Present
    *   *Note: Appointed officially on July 14, 2023 (with the inauguration ceremony held on August 3, 2023), he remains in office as of late 2024.*

# Lista de ministros do Turismo do Brasil

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros do Turismo](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_do_Turismo_(Brasil) "Ministério do Turismo (Brasil)")** do [Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil "Brasil").

De 19 de outubro de 1992, no governo do presidente [Itamar Franco](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") até o início do segundo governo do presidente [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso"), em 1 de janeiro de 1999, o ministério era denominado Ministério de Indústria, Comércio e Turismo. A partir de então foi denominado Ministério do Esporte e Turismo, até o início do primeiro mandato do presidente [Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva"), em 1 de janeiro de 2003, quando foi denominado simplesmente Ministério do Turismo.

The **Ministry of Tourism** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério do Turismo*) is a [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil")-level [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_institutions_of_Brazil "List of federal institutions of Brazil") created on 1 January 2003. It is responsible for [Embratur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embratur "Embratur"), the Brazilian Tourist Board.

Developing tourism as a sustainable economic activity with a relevant role for the [generation of jobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment "Unemployment") and [foreign currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currency "Currency") and providing [social inclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_exclusion "Social exclusion"). The Ministry of Tourism is innovating in the handling of public policies with a decentralized management model, guided by [strategic thinking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_thinking "Strategic thinking").

Its organizational structure comprises the National Secretariat of Tourism Policies, which assumes the role of carrying out the [national policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Policy "National Policy") for the sector, oriented by the directives from the national Council of Tourism. In addition, it is responsible for the internal promotion and oversees the [quality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quality_assurance "Quality assurance") of the provision of the Brazilian tourism service.

The National Secretariat of Programs for the Development of Tourism is responsible for subsidizing the formulation of plans, programs and actions for the strengthening of national tourism. The duties of the body are the promotion and development of [infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure "Infrastructure") and the improvement in the quality of the services rendered.

[EMBRATUR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embratur "Embratur") – Brazilian Tourism Institute, established on November 18, 1966, as a Brazilian tourism enterprise, had the objective of fostering tourism activity by making feasible conditions for the generation of jobs, income and development throughout the country.

Since January 2003, upon the establishment of the Ministry of Tourism, EMBRATUR's actions were concentrated in the promotion, marketing and support to the trading of products, services and tourism destinations.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Tourism_(Brazil)#cite_note-MTUR-2)

| Website | [www.gov.br/turismo/](https://www.gov.br/turismo/) |

The **Ministry of Tourism** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério do Turismo*) is a [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil")-level [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_institutions_of_Brazil "List of federal institutions of Brazil") created on 1 January 2003. It is responsible for [Embratur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embratur "Embratur"), the Brazilian Tourist Board.

Developing tourism as a sustainable economic activity with a relevant role for the [generation of jobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment "Unemployment") and [foreign currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currency "Currency") and providing [social inclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_exclusion "Social exclusion"). The Ministry of Tourism is innovating in the handling of public policies with a decentralized management model, guided by [strategic thinking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_thinking "Strategic thinking").

Its organizational structure comprises the National Secretariat of Tourism Policies, which assumes the role of carrying out the [national policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Policy "National Policy") for the sector, oriented by the directives from the national Council of Tourism. In addition, it is responsible for the internal promotion and oversees the [quality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quality_assurance "Quality assurance") of the provision of the Brazilian tourism service.

The National Secretariat of Programs for the Development of Tourism is responsible for subsidizing the formulation of plans, programs and actions for the strengthening of national tourism. The duties of the body are the promotion and development of [infrastructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure "Infrastructure") and the improvement in the quality of the services rendered.

[EMBRATUR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embratur "Embratur") – Brazilian Tourism Institute, established on November 18, 1966, as a Brazilian tourism enterprise, had the objective of fostering tourism activity by making feasible conditions for the generation of jobs, income and development throughout the country.

Since January 2003, upon the establishment of the Ministry of Tourism, EMBRATUR's actions were concentrated in the promotion, marketing and support to the trading of products, services and tourism destinations.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Tourism_(Brazil)#cite_note-MTUR-2)

# Lista de ministros do Turismo do Brasil

Esta é uma **lista de [ministros do Turismo](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minist%C3%A9rio_do_Turismo_(Brasil) "Ministério do Turismo (Brasil)")** do [Brasil](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brasil "Brasil").

De 19 de outubro de 1992, no governo do presidente [Itamar Franco](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") até o início do segundo governo do presidente [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso"), em 1 de janeiro de 1999, o ministério era denominado Ministério de Indústria, Comércio e Turismo. A partir de então foi denominado Ministério do Esporte e Turismo, até o início do primeiro mandato do presidente [Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva"), em 1 de janeiro de 2003, quando foi denominado simplesmente Ministério do Turismo.

He was **temporarily exonerated** on **December 2, 2024**, to resume his mandate as a Federal Deputy in the Chamber of Deputies, likely to vote on parliamentary amendments or budgetary matters—a common practice for Brazilian ministers who are also elected lawmakers. *   **End of 2024:** He closed the year as Minister of Tourism.

**Answer:** Yes, effectively, though he underwent a brief, temporary exoneration in **December 2024** for legislative purposes before being reinstated.

Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Tourism from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024:

**Under President Michel Temer (2018 term)**
*   **Marx Beltrão**
    *   *Period:* Served from the start of 2018 until April 10, 2018.
    *   *Note:* He originally took office in 2016 and resigned in April 2018 to run for legislative office.
*   **Vinicius Lummertz**
    *   *Period:* April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018.

**Under President Jair Bolsonaro (2019–2022)**
*   **Marcelo Álvaro Antônio**
    *   *Period:* January 1, 2019 – December 9, 2020.
*   **Gilson Machado Neto**
    *   *Period:* December 9, 2020 – March 31, 2022.
    *   *Note:* Resigned to run for the Senate.
*   **Carlos Brito**
    *   *Period:* March 31, 2022 – December 31, 2022.

**Under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (2023–2024)**
*   **Daniela Carneiro** (also known as Daniela do Waguinho)
    *   *Period:* January 1, 2023 – July 14, 2023.
*   **Celso Sabino**
    *   *Period:* July 14, 2023 – End of 2024.
    *   *Note:* Sabino remained in office through the end of 2024, though he was briefly and technically exonerated in early December 2024 to vote on matters in Congress before being reinstated.

full_history.response:
Here is the list of Brazilian Ministers of Tourism from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024:

**Under President Michel Temer (2018 term)**
*   **Marx Beltrão**
    *   *Period:* Served from the start of 2018 until April 10, 2018.
    *   *Note:* He originally took office in 2016 and resigned in April 2018 to run for legislative office.
*   **Vinicius Lummertz**
    *   *Period:* April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018.

**Under President Jair Bolsonaro (2019–2022)**
*   **Marcelo Álvaro Antônio**
    *   *Period:* January 1, 2019 – December 9, 2020.
*   **Gilson Machado Neto**
    *   *Period:* December 9, 2020 – March 31, 2022.
    *   *Note:* Resigned to run for the Senate.
*   **Carlos Brito**
    *   *Period:* March 31, 2022 – December 31, 2022.

**Under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (2023–2024)**
*   **Daniela Carneiro** (also known as Daniela do Waguinho)
    *   *Period:* January 1, 2023 – July 14, 2023.
*   **Celso Sabino**
    *   *Period:* July 14, 2023 – End of 2024.
    *   *Note:* Sabino remained in office through the end of 2024, though he was briefly and technically exonerated in early December 2024 to vote on matters in Congress before being reinstated.
